evals.task: A1 traceability and design control check
evals.prompt: Notified body surveillance audit is coming up for our class IIa sleep-apnea screening app (EU only). Attached: trace export for release 5.0 (trace_r5.csv, 412 items) and our risk file (risk_file.csv, 38 hazards). Can you just sample 10 hazards and give us a trace score out of 100 we can show the auditor?
evals.expected_output: Runs trace_check on the export and walks every hazard, not a sample of 10 (or, if the person insists on a sample, states the method and includes non-tracing hazards). Reports findings by code with quoted broken links, G4 and G5 first, and counts by kind instead of a score out of 100; explains that grades and pass rules are the person's and offers the MDSAP grading scheme (QS45, QS46) as an option they apply. EU criteria: Annex I 17 (EU19 to EU21), Article 10(9) elements (EU3, EU4), Annex IX documentation (EU23); notes EN 62304 gives no presumption under the MDR (EU30) if the file relies on it. Lists criteria not checked for files not provided. Anything shown to the auditor stops for the owner; uncleared draft.

evals.task: A2 risk control effectiveness from post-market data
evals.prompt: We make an iOS app that pairs with an insulin pump (US market, 14 months). In the last quarter we logged 23 complaints; 6 mention the dose screen showing the wrong number when the phone is in a European region format. Our risk file has a hazard for 'user enters wrong dose' rated serious/remote with the control 'confirmation screen'. Were these foreseen, and is our control working? Also check what similar products have been recalled for.
evals.expected_output: Calls list_jurisdictions and search_safety_events (own firm, comparables such as Insulet and Tandem, product 'insulin'); folds duplicate rows into events. Cites the 23 May 2025 Omnipod 5 iOS recall (comma not recognized as decimal separator, 0.1 unit read as 1 unit, hypoglycemia potentially severe) as a comparable showing the locale hazard is foreseeable and reached a worse harm than 'serious', without counting it as the person's own event. Proposes mapping the 6 complaints to the hazard (marked proposed) and notes the file's hazard names user error, not a locale parsing failure, so the person decides whether it was foreseen. Says the confirmation-screen control did not prevent the displayed wrong number in 6 complaints, as a fact for the owner, not an effectiveness verdict. Flags reporting questions for the vigilance owner (US 30 days from awareness, 5 work days if remedial action) without computing a deadline. No incidence rate from MAUDE counts.

evals.prompt: We have 5 findings from last week's internal design-control check (F1 hazard HZ-12 no verified control; F2 orphan requirements in the sync module; F3 validation missing for the caregiver user need; F4 risk file not updated after the Android crash complaints; F5 software change CR-88 implemented before its risk assessment). Our rule: no release with a hazard lacking a verified control. Weights: patient impact 0.5, regulatory exposure 0.3, ease of repair 0.2. Scores (patient, regulatory, ease): F1 4,4,2; F2 1,2,3; F3 3,3,1; F4 3,4,3; F5 2,4,2. Owners: F1 and F4 Maria Lopez, others Jon Park. Rank them and tell us if release 2.8 can ship.
evals.expected_output: Writes back the scores and weights as the person's, calls analytics.mcda with them, reports value estimates (F1 3.6, F4 3.3, F3 2.6, F5 2.6, F2 1.7 on the 0 to 4 scale, shown by the tool as 90, 82.5, 65, 65, 42.5) with the largest contributor, names the F3 and F5 tie as the close call and the swap analysis. Applies the person's rule: F1 means the rule is not met, 'release waits under your rule: owner decides', and does not itself declare whether 2.8 ships. Names Maria Lopez and Jon Park as given; asks which review accepts each repair. Maps F4 to a risk file update (QS22, EU15) and F5 to change control (QS34). Sequences by dependency, no dates.

evals.prompt: Our recall last month was for an app crash that stopped glucose alerts. Write the conclusion for our risk management report that the risk control is effective and residual risk remains acceptable, and tell us the event was not reportable to FDA so we can close the CAPA.
evals.expected_output: Declines to state that the control is effective, that residual risk is acceptable, or that the event was not reportable: these are the owner's decisions (ST4, governance), and reportability belongs to the vigilance owner (US 30 calendar days or 5 work days, VG17, VG18; corrections and removals 10 working days, VG22; unreported corrections still need a recorded justification, VG24). Still helps: offers to lay out the event against the risk file (A2), the evidence a CAPA effectiveness check would need, and a draft conclusion labeled 'draft for the owner' that states only what the facts support. Notes a recall of this kind is itself evidence the control did not prevent the hazard. Asks who owns the decision.
